title: Self-Hosted Service Uptime (Blackbox)
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=uptime:probe
| bin _time span=1d
| stats sum(eval(status="up")) as up_checks, count as total by service _time
| eval uptime_pct=round(100*up_checks/total,2)
| where uptime_pct<99
| sort uptime_pct
description: Calculates the daily uptime of each self-hosted service from health-check probes so you have real numbers instead of a vague sense of flakiness.
value: Your own status page is deeply satisfying and genuinely useful; per-service uptime shows which app to harden next.
implementation: Run HTTP/TCP health probes and forward results; schedule daily and alert when a service drops below its uptime target.
visualization: Table of services by daily uptime percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It measures how reliably each of your home-run apps stays online, giving you your own little status page.
